title: The NSFNET Backbone SPF Based Interior Gateway Protocol
publisher_or_issuer: Network Working Group / RFC archival corpus
redistribution_notes: Prefer RFC Editor canonical text and metadata.

claims_extracted.claim: The 1988 NSFNET backbone connected thirteen continental-US sites with permanent point-to-point T1 links at 1.544 Mbit/s.
T1 facilities could contain multiple logical links at sub-T1 through full-T1 rates, creating a hybrid circuit/packet-switched topology richer than the physical topology.
Each site had an NSS, a RISC multiprocessor system using IBM RT/PC processors and a modified 4.3BSD kernel.
claims_extracted.notes: RFC treats the NSS as one logical routing entity and does not enumerate all physical processors.

claims_extracted.claim: Inter-NSS routing used an adaptation of ANSI IS-IS; attached mid-level networks used EGP with policy restrictions.
The implementation documented 10-second IS-ES Hello intervals and 40-second hold time.
claims_extracted.notes: Treat as this documented implementation's parameters, not timeless NSFNET constants.

notes: Contemporary protocol evidence for logical NSS architecture. Pair with Merit Figure 14 for physical processor-role decomposition.
